title: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

sense.text:
Today’s topic is learning to see with spiritual eyes.

“Arise, shine”: that means wake up from your sleep. Arise and shine, wake up and teach; shine right there refers to teach. “For thy light is come”: Christ has come, understanding has come. “And the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee”: the holy spirit is upon each and every one of us.

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth”: this is where we are at right now. Darkness has covered the earth.

“And gross darkness the people”: the worst kind of darkness. When it says the people, it is referring to the people of God, the Israelites. Sure, the whole world’s in darkness, but we have the worst kind of darkness there is. Why? Because we’ve lost our identity, our language, our culture, our heritage, our customs, our land. We’ve lost one another, we’ve lost our people, we’ve lost our minds.

Like when you get a check: there’s the net of your check and the gross of the check, and the gross is the whole thing without taxes coming out. In terms of darkness, we got the gross darkness; the nations got the net, we got the gross.

“But the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee”: the Lord shall arise upon us.

precepts.why:
Another term for this darkness. The chapter is the fall of Babylon, but this one verse shows what it calls America, Babylon the great: “The city of confusion is broken down”. The Bible calls this place the city of confusion. This whole country is the city of confusion, where women lead the men, the men are effeminate, men transforming into women, women transforming into men. This city, Babylon the great, is the city of confusion, and God said it’s broken down.

“Every house is shut up”, and there is a crying in the streets. “All joy is darkened”: that’s why it says gross darkness the people. “The mirth of the land is gone.”

sense.text:
Another metaphor on this darkness, on this confusion. “And the great dragon was cast out”: the great dragon, which is Satan. “That old serpent”: why did it say that old serpent? Because it’s the same serpent from the past. “Called the Devil, and Satan”: this is the white man right here.

Why say the Devil and Satan is the white man? Not because of some racist innuendo; because God said it, Christ said it, in Revelation 2.

“Which deceiveth the whole world”: you think there’s a spirit flowing around deceiving everybody? No. It’s the educational system that’s been set up, the school system, the church system, the media. All those things are tools of Satan to deceive the whole world, and the physical counterpart is the white man. That’s why the Apostle Paul writes in Thessalonians that the mystery of iniquity was already at work: the power of sin in a kingdom was already rolling, already in power. It’s not some mythical thing flying around; the Satan-structured system is all around us at work.

The American empire and its media: the Council of Foreign Relations controls the media; CNN, the New York Times, Fox, NBC, CBS, NPR. There’s no black men or black women running that; this ain’t our people. Byron Allen tried to buy Comcast and they said he can’t buy it. Bill Cosby tried to buy NBC; they said he’s getting beside himself, and they brought up rape charges, and some of y’all went with that and didn’t see the ulterior motive behind it. Nate Parker did Birth of a Nation and his career was fine until he wanted to do Nat Turner; then they brought up all those accusations against him. There is a pattern to the way this white man runs things. The media “deceiveth the whole world.”

“He was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him”: all his allies were cast out with him.

precepts.why:
This is why the white man is called the devil and Satan: Christ said this. “I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not”. Well, if they’re not Jews, who are they? “But are the synagogue of Satan”. Jesus Christ called them Satan.

Read on. He tells the Israelites, don’t fear what you’re going to suffer: “behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison”. Rome was casting us into prison. What did Christ call Rome? The devil.

So who’s going around this world today saying that they’re the Jews, that they’re Jewish? It’s the white man. You say we’re taking it out of context; you’re simple as hell.

This is talking about idolatry: it tells how idols came into the earth. A man who was a king, a leader, had a son that he loved, and an artist wanted to please the king. “For he, peradventure willing to please one in authority, forced all his skill to make the resemblance of the best fashion. And so the multitude, allured by the grace of the work, took him now for a god, which a little before was but honoured”. The artist took the image of the king’s son and made him an image of a god, and everybody started thinking that son was God.

“And this was an occasion to deceive the world”: didn’t we just read in Revelation 12:9 about that great dragon called the Devil and Satan, “which deceiveth the whole world”? “For men, serving either calamity or tyranny, did ascribe unto stones and stocks the incommunicable name”: they said this is God, that is God, that’s the Almighty.

“But whereas they lived in the great war of ignorance, those so great plagues called they peace.” They called those plagues of ignorance peace. Living in ignorance is not peace, because something comes behind that ignorance, and the next verses break it down. “For whilst they slew their children in sacrifices”: they were having abortions, killing their babies, and they thought that was peace. “Or used secret ceremonies, or made revellings of strange rites; They kept neither lives nor marriages any longer undefiled”: this is our people even until this day. “Or grieved him by adultery”: like the holidays where one woman leaves her husband and sleeps with another man, and the man gets another woman.

“So that there reigned in all men without exception”: all races were guilty of this, “blood, manslaughter, theft, and dissimulation, corruption, unfaithfulness, tumults”, “disquieting of good men, forgetfulness of good turns, defiling of souls, changing of kind”: transforming men into women, women into men. “Disorder in marriages, adultery, and shameless uncleanness.” They called all this peace. All these things we’re reading, we see in real life, and people on the street say this is a good society, we’re all at peace, why are you Israelites causing division? Just by us reading the Bible, they believe we’re the problem.

“For the worshipping of idols not to be named is the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil.” Verse 27 is so deep: it tells you the first sin, with Adam and Eve, was idolatry, and the last sin in the world will be idolatry.

An example of a man that took the image of a boy and made that boy into a god: in the book called The Pillory, the bust of the Savior was posed for by Caesar Borgia, the second son of Pope Alexander the sixth of Rome. They made him into the image of God. The original of the bust was found in a church of San Salvatore, now destroyed, and it is an open secret that Caesar Borgia posed for it. Open secret means white folks know about it; blacks and Latinos, our people, are the ones in gross darkness. We have become the dumbest people on the planet when it comes to learning, education and what’s going on in the world. Another book calls him the firstborn son of Alexander the sixth, but the point is this: Leonardo da Vinci was the first one to paint his image as Jesus Christ, followed by Michelangelo, who was younger. Those were the two main artists that painted Caesar Borgia as Jesus Christ, and there are Leonardo da Vinci’s own sketches of him.

And our people will kill you for this image; they will shoot you, they will stab you. In Sierra Leone, Deacon Isaac stepped on that picture and a black woman fell on the ground crying in hysteria. Captain Abiel was in Queens where our people were worshipping Guadalupe, and they threw hot water out the window and threw rocks at the brothers for this evil image. Black Christians, Latino Christians, you cannot battle against the Israelites: not only do we know the Bible, we have historical evidence to shut you down. Every last Catholic church, Baptist church, Jehovah Witness, Seventh-Day Adventist: all your churches are garbage, because they cannot dispute this evidence.

“Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many.” The Jesuit priests, the missionaries: they were the many that went throughout Santo Domingo, Puerto Rico, Latin America, Central America, North America. They went throughout the world saying they are Christ, these images of Caesar Borgia. Disprove that, Christians; prove me a liar. Images are very important.

Our people will kill you for that evil image of death around their necks. A sister said, I don’t worship it, it’s just a representation of Jesus. No, sister, that’s an idol, because the Catholic church is the one that pushed that doctrine of wearing it around your neck for a spiritual blessing. Where in the Bible did any of them say wear that on your neck? Chapter, scripture and verse: crickets. Christians are evil and stupid and violent; they live in the great war of ignorance.

sense.text:
In this great darkness, this gross darkness we all live in, we need spiritual eyes to see. Our spiritual eye is our spiritual understanding, and that’s also called the holy spirit in the Bible. “Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures”: you need your understanding opened that you might understand the scriptures.

Not only do you need to know who you are, you need to know who the devil is. If you can’t figure out those two things, your spiritual eyes will be closed and you will never understand the scriptures; you’ll be talking about there’s some good white folks and some bad ones. Where is that in the Bible? It don’t say that.

precepts.why: “In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother.” This goes back to the history of Cain and Abel, the history of Jacob and Esau. Just as God has his children manifest on earth, Satan has his children manifest on earth too. Knowing who the devil is opens the understanding.

sense.text:
The question is how do you get the Holy Spirit, how do you get your spiritual eyes open, how do you get your understanding open to understand the scriptures. “If ye love me, keep my commandments.” That is the stipulation to get the Holy Spirit: in order to get that Spirit of truth, brothers and sisters, you must be keeping the commandments.

Growing up in church there was a class where you could learn to get the Holy Spirit, and the man would have everybody say see my tie, say it faster, say it again, and put it together. That’s stupid black Christian stuff, stupid and evil: ninety-nine percent of them in there are black and Latin women, and the rest are black effeminate men and Latin men doing that garbage.

“He shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth”. We all want that Spirit of truth. “Whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not”: the world doesn’t see Christ, “neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.”
“I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.” Christ lets you know his spirit is the Comforter; that Holy Spirit is his spirit.

precepts.why: Proverbs says the same thing. “Turn you at my reproof”: reproof means keep the commandments, God’s reproof with his commandments. “Behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you”: that’s how you get the Holy Spirit. It was true in the past the same way, the same thing Christ said; there’s no other way.

sense.text: “But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost”: it gives you another term for the Comforter. The Spirit of truth was called the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, the Holy Ghost. “He shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.” The Holy Ghost would bring all things to our remembrance, whatsoever Christ said to us, and Christ said a lot of things to the children of Israel.

precepts.why: One of the main things Christ said, that the churches don’t read and don’t want to talk about. “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the Israelites would fall by the sword, the Roman sword, “and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” Christ said the Israelites would all go into slavery and the other nations would live in Jerusalem. The churches that claim they got the Holy Spirit: the Holy Spirit never showed them that. You mean to tell me the Holy Spirit never told them that?

“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments”. One of the first things to get a good understanding of the Bible: you must do the commandments. A lot of these discombobulated Christians don’t do the commandments, so they don’t understand the Bible, but they put on good talk like they do. When you examine them precept upon precept, they don’t know what the hell they’re talking about.

sense.text: “The light of the body is the eye”: that eye is your spiritual eye. “If therefore thine eye be single”: if your spiritual eye be focused, focused on what God says, “thy whole body shall be full of light”: your whole body shall be full of God’s light, his law.

“But if thine eye be evil”: if your spiritual eye within you be evil, “thy whole body shall be full of darkness”, your whole body is wicked as hell. “If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!”

So you find the children of light and the children of darkness, which is like what we read in 1 John 3:10, the children of God and the children of the devil: it’s saying the same thing. We got to learn to open our spiritual eyes.

Our people held up signs in the 50s and 60s: wipe out poverty, stop police brutality, stop racist brutality. You may say that was back in the 60s and has nothing to do with us today, but Sandra Bland, George Floyd, Tamir Rice: you thought police brutality was just back then? And some were not killed by the police at all: Trayvon Martin was not killed by the police. There’s a narrative the Black Lives movement is trying to spin, that it’s only the police doing it. No. God says the nation of Esau has a perpetual hatred.

“Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred”: the word perpetual means everlasting, “and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end”. Every time we got emancipated, the white man came with his perpetual hatred against us. So the Bible says it ain’t just the police; the system is trying to get you to look at just the police, but it’s white folks. Stop murder by police is a false narrative.

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Edom”: Edom means red, red people, “and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof”. God said he will not turn away their punishment, “because he did pursue his brother with the sword”: he pursued the Israelites with the sword, “and did cast off all pity”: he cast off all pity from us, “and his anger did tear perpetually”: there you go again, perpetually, “and he kept his wrath for ever”.

Don’t say it’s the police. The Bible says Esau, Edom; we got to speak what the Bible says. Stop following stupid Black Lives Matter people; most of them are lesbians and homosexuals.

sense.text:
Deuteronomy 28:15-68 talks about slavery, colonialism, loss of identity and oppression. Loss of identity: when we ask blacks and Latinos on the street what’s your nationality, who are you in the Bible, they all get the same stupid look. I’m a child of God; well, God had one race of people as his children, which one is it? Then they want to fight you, curse your mama, smack the Bible out your hand. Don’t care how much money they got, they don’t know who they are; this is what Christ calls our people, the spiritual poor.

Oppression: our people held up signs in the turbulent 50s and 60s, race discrimination breeds fascism; we came back from the war good enough to drive your tanks, why not the trolleys? Don’t buy where you can’t work: even back then they had sense. You can’t tell our people that today. In Chicago, when brothers went to protest after a black woman and her daughter were beaten, black women gathered and cursed the men out for standing up for them. Sisters, a lot of you don’t deserve to be protected; you’re bovine excrement, no damn good.

“But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”. God said if you break my commandments curses will come upon you. He didn’t say if you break the white man’s religion, if you stop going to church on Sunday, if you don’t go to church on fake Christmas or Mother’s Day. The churches haven’t figured this out; their spiritual eyes are still closed.
“Cursed shalt thou be in the city”: whatever city our people live in, we are under God’s curse. “And cursed shalt thou be in the field”: wherever we are in the world, we are cursed.

“Cursed shall be thy basket and thy store.” Jay Morrison, Black Wall Street: him, Dr Boyce Watkins and other black entrepreneurs were getting their money together and buying property, and they bought a big building in Georgia, the Legacy Center. Then, allegedly (allegedly, because I’m not in that circle and don’t know), he stole all the money, and they sold it. The people got robbed and the people are angry, and rightfully so. That explains Deuteronomy 28:17: cursed shall be thy basket and thy store.

“Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body”: many of your children, “and the fruit of thy land, the increase of thy kine, and the flocks of thy sheep. Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and cursed shalt thou be when thou goest out.”

precepts.why: “And if ye be born, ye shall be born to a curse”: you don’t know who you are, you don’t know what your purpose in life is. “And if ye die, a curse shall be your portion”: if you grow old and die, you still won’t know who you are or what your purpose was upon the earth. You still fall under God’s curses, cursed coming in and cursed going out.

sense.text:
“And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness”: there is that word darkness again. Remember, gross darkness the people; we are in gross darkness. We’re like blind men, blind women: we can’t see the truth, we can’t handle the truth. We’re looking for democracy to save us, Christianity to save us, Biden to save us, Trump, white Jesus to save us.

“And thou shalt not prosper in thy ways”: some of you say, well, I’m financially stable. That’s not what the Bible is talking about; it’s talking about us as a people not prospering. We’re the only race that talks me, me, me. All races on earth work collectively except dumb blacks and Latinos; we’re the only ones that cannot work together. We are all discombobulated, we can’t function as a nation, and then we wonder why the nations disrespect us: because you have no loyalty amongst one another.

“And thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.” Christians ain’t figured that out. Ask why our people are oppressed and they say, I’m not oppressed, I got a good job, I got a nice little house in the Poconos. Christians can’t explain it to this day, and Muslims can’t explain it either. Deuteronomy 28 is one of the easiest chapters in the Bible to understand; if your friends and family can’t see what it is saying, their spiritual eyes are closed.

What the Most High is saying about our particular darkness, which is gross darkness: “And thou shalt grope at noonday”. That goes right back to what we read in Isaiah about the gross darkness. Groping around means you can’t see; you’re feeling on the walls trying to find your way, and we are groping in the bright light. “As the blind gropeth in darkness”: can a blind man see? Put a blind man in a dark room; that’s how blind we are when the sun is straight up in the sky. That’s some serious blindness, like we never had eyes.

precepts.why: This was written to the Israelites in Rome; it’s talking about us. “And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep”. High time is noon time. Are you supposed to be asleep when the sun is straight up at noon? Everybody’s supposed to be awake. So who is he speaking to? The people that’s in gross darkness, groping at noonday.

sense.text: “And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee”: meaning we would lose our identity. We would be relabeled. One of the curses that sums up Deuteronomy is loss of identity.

precepts.why: The precept to explain that verse: we lost our minds. “And ye shall leave your name for a curse unto my chosen”: we left the name of Israel for a curse. Now we’re African-American, Dominican, Haitian, Jamaican, Honduran; those are curses. “For the Lord God shall slay thee, and call his servants by another name”.

sense.text: Christians often say those curses don’t fit today. Really? “The stranger that is within thee”: the other nations, “shall get up above thee very high”: the Chinese, the white man, the Arabs got up above us very high. “And thou shalt come down very low”: we’ve come down very low in society.

“He shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him”: who owns the bank, who’s doing the lending, who is sending out foreign aid to nations? It’s the white man. It’s not Africa, it ain’t Latin America. “He shall be the head”: the white man shall be the head, “and thou shalt be the tail”, the tail of all nations.
“Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed”, because we refuse to keep the commandments.

“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder”: those same curses would be upon us for a sign that we are the children of God, we are the Israelites. “And upon thy seed for ever”: how long? Forever. It didn’t say it ended with the Roman captivity, like these stupid Urban apologetics like to say, that all the curses ended with Rome. That’s a lie; that’s not Bible.

“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness”: we didn’t have joy in us to keep God’s laws, “and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”: the abundance of us ruling the planet earth. We were supposed to rule the planet earth, and we lost it all, we lost everything.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies”: you shall serve the white man, the Arabs, Iraq, Iran, India, Pakistan, “which the Lord shall send against thee”: the Lord sent those nations against us. “In hunger”: to serve those same nations for food; “in thirst”: for water; “in nakedness”: for clothing; “and in want of all things”: that includes birth certificates, social security, death certificates, hospitalization, medicine, education. Even if you want to learn about God, you got to go to your enemies to teach you about religion. “And he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck”: we had yokes of iron on our necks as evidence that this is talking about our people, “until he have destroyed thee”, until we were destroyed as a people, as a race.

Summed up, Deuteronomy 28:15-68 is slavery, colonialism, loss of identity and oppression.

“So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun”: Solomon saw a vision of all the oppressions done under the sun, the oppressions upon the Israelites. “And behold the tears of such as were oppressed”: our people are filled with tears. Our mothers and sisters and aunts, we see them cry a lot; if you grew up in poverty, you’ve seen your mother cry for the lack of food. “And they had no comforter”: the Holy Spirit was not with us.

“And on the side of their oppressors there was power”: on the side of the white man and these other nations there was power; there was Satan, there was the devil. “But they had no comforter.”

What kind of power do they have? They make laws: the legislative branch, the Senate and the House of Representatives. You may say there’s some Latinos and blacks in there; they don’t pass no laws. They’re there to support, as managers, as faces to fool the masses of the people. Our enemies have power, and they are the ones that institutionalize oppression: institutional racism, structural racism, environmental racism, colorism, racial profiling, economic discrimination, mass incarceration, education disparities, health inequities and housing discrimination, redlining among them. All of this comes from the legislative branch; they back all these things and don’t come against them. We could spend all day talking about just one of them alone.

Another example of power: America has the largest and most powerful military on the earth, and they even have a police force of 40,000 here in New York. Behind their legislative branch all of this backs them up, so you’re not overthrowing them. King Solomon was prophesying in the spirit. The things we see in the Bible, Christians can never see; their spiritual eyes are closed, and all they see is give me money.

precepts.why:
On the side of the oppressors there is power, but there’s something behind these afflictions we get. “He delivereth the poor in his affliction”: God delivers the poor in his affliction, “and openeth their ears in oppression”: he opens their spiritual ears in oppression.

So you might ask yourself, what good has oppression done us? Oppression allows us to hear the word of God. Oppression allows the Comforter to speak wisdom into dead, sleeping spirits. When you’re oppressed you’re looking for answers, and now you know not to go looking in all the wrong places: going to church, where they tell you about the love of the white man that’s gonna save you, when he’s the one oppressing you; looking to Biden, and Biden is the one oppressing us; looking to the government, and the legislative branch is the one oppressing us.

“I will go and return to my place”: the Lord said I will go and return to the heavens, “till they acknowledge their offence”: until the twelve tribes of Israel acknowledge their sins, breaking his commandments. “And seek my face”: get their face in that Bible, seek the Lord. “In their affliction they will seek me early.” When we start getting afflicted, we start seeking the Lord.

And there’s going to be more affliction on our people. The Bible prophesies that one third of Israel is going to be delivered, and one third ain’t even repented yet, so more affliction is going to come, whether through earthquakes, storms, or oppression coming through the government. So don’t be shocked, don’t be dismayed. Our people must be afflicted so that they will acknowledge their offences and hear the word of God.

sense.text: Our people must be afflicted so that they will acknowledge their offences and hear the word of God. Then comes this: “And the eyes of them that see shall not be dim”. The eyes of them that see what? The words of God. They shall not be dim no more. “And the ears of them that hear shall hearken”: they shall hearken and obey. Hear and see what? The word of God.

precepts.why:
“And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book”: we are the spiritual deaf, hearing the words of the book. What book? The Bible, the same book in your hands. “And the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity, and out of darkness”: what eyes? Our spiritual eyes. And the eyes of the blind, that’s us.

So when we started in Isaiah 60 about the gross darkness, now our spiritual eyes and spiritual ears are being opened to the words of the book. The book is the Holy Bible. The book is not the Quran, the book is not the Egyptian Book of the Dead, the book is not the Gilgamesh epics. The book is the Bible, the word of God.

“The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling”. The only way to know what the hope of God’s calling is, is for our spiritual eyes to be opened. And in order for them to be opened we must be oppressed, we must go through oppression and affliction. That’s what pushes us into this truth, that’s what pushes us to now see the Bible and say, oh, this is what it’s talking about. Because now the Holy Spirit can say, now I can dwell with you, now I can work with you.

“And what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints, And what is the exceeding greatness of his power to us-ward who believe, according to the working of his mighty power”. So now we see the greatness of his power to us-ward who believe. Now we understand in portion, because we don’t know everything.

“Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” This is why every time we read the Bible we always come across something we never saw. We read it before, but we didn’t see it with our spiritual eyes. King David says open thou mine eyes: what eyes? My spiritual eyes.

So now when we read the law, the four chapters a day, day by day by day, once you finish through that year you go through the next. Now you’re reading the same things and you go, you know what, I read this last year, I never saw that part though. More stuff starts to come out, because your spiritual eyes are opening.

Like in the movie The Matrix: when they woke Neo up out of that chamber he said my eyes hurt, and they said, you never used them. That’s the same thing with us: we’ve never used our spiritual eyes.

Watch what Christ says: “I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich”. He’s counseling us to buy of him gold tried in the fire, and that gold tried in the fire is the word of God, that the prophets died to write and put together. “And white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed”: that white raiment is a celestial body. “And that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear”: that our sin don’t appear.

“And anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see.” We’re anointing our eyes with the word of God, so that we may see this darkness, this gross darkness that we live in now. Oh no, you’re not fooling me with that; I hear the music, that music is evil. Your spiritual ears are open now; you need to anoint your eyes with the word of God.

sense.text: That Bible breaks up the grip of Christianity. “The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.” David said the Lord is my shepherd. When we think of a shepherd, we visualize in our mind a man with a shepherd’s staff around sheep. But what it’s really talking about is Christ. Christ is the shepherd, we are the sheep. Christ is the king, and we are actually the sheep.

precepts.why:
“I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.” He’s explaining it: what you read about the shepherd in the book of Psalms, Christ said, that’s me, I’m the good shepherd.

“But he that is an hireling, and not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not”: the sheep, the Israelites, don’t belong to a hireling. He “seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth: and the wolf catcheth them, and scattereth the sheep. The hireling fleeth, because he is an hireling, and careth not for the sheep.”

That’s Christianity, that’s these religious organizations: they’re hirelings, they’re temporary. Even you, once you examine yourself, will determine whether or not you are a hireling in this truth. When we saw a lot of danger around us, the BBC, the SPLC against us, some brothers fled the truth. They saw the wolf coming and they ran for the hills: hirelings. And these ministers, look at them, they got Tyler Perry. Come on with this foolishness.

Christ comes back again: “I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine. As the Father knoweth me, even so know I the Father: and I lay down my life for the sheep.” Christ said, I lay down my life for the sheep; I’ll give my life for the Israelites.

“And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold”: he said, I got all the sheep, all the Israelites, which are not here in Israel today. “Them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.” Christians will use verse 16 and go, see, other sheep means all nations, every other. No, it ain’t talking about that. Why does it say one fold and one shepherd? Ezekiel 37:22 is the precept.

This is why it says one fold and one shepherd: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”. The two nations are the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom.

So that’s why Christ said, other sheep I have which are not of this fold. They are not all nations; they are the rest of Israel, brought together under the one shepherd.

We’re still dealing with the Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want. “Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant”. Our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd: he’s the one in the Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want.
“And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away.” When the chief Shepherd shall appear: that’s Christ. He is the chief Shepherd.

“Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock”: he that leads the northern kingdom like a flock. Now you might say that’s just talking about Joseph, or Ephraim. Watch who he’s talking about: “thou that dwellest between the cherubims, shine forth.” That ain’t Joseph dwelling between the cherubims; that’s Christ that dwells between the cherubims.

See, the northern kingdom ain’t forgotten. The Lord ain’t forgot them; he said, I’m going to lead them too. That goes with what we just read: other sheep I have. So he’s going to lead the northern kingdom, Joseph.

“He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young”. This is what the Lord is going to do.

Start at verse 10: “Behold, the Lord God will come with strong hand, and his arm shall rule for him: behold, his reward is with him, and his work before him.” Then he shall feed his flock like a shepherd. You see that: that’s how gentle the Lord is going to deal with us. Now we know who that shepherd is in Psalms 23:1.

sense.text: “The Lord is my shepherd”: now we know who that shepherd is. “I shall not want”: I shall not lack. Want means lack, or fall short of.

precepts.why: I shall not lack. “The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame.” Brothers and sisters, understand these are the chief things in life that we all need. We all need water, we all need bread, food, we all need clothing, and an house to cover shame. Those are the four chief principal things that we need in life, and that’s what we shall not want.

“But godliness with contentment is great gain.” Content with what? Water, food, clothing and shelter. “For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.” You see what it says: food and raiment, the principal things we read earlier in Sirach. Let us be therewith content.

David said, “I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken”. That’s the righteous: those men and women keeping God’s commandments, involved in the work of God. I said that for a reason. “Nor his seed begging bread.” Why? Because Israel works as a collective, and the Lord will bless us as a collective.

Working as a collective: “Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold, And laid them down at the apostles’ feet: and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need.”

Those men that distribution was given to, whether they were single or had families, were doing the work. They wasn’t just sitting around asking, got a dollar, got five dollars, and not doing nothing. Those were men involved in God’s work; everybody could speak on their work.

I’m saying that because you always get that one grimy that comes around. He ain’t about nothing, he don’t do nothing, but his hand is always out: I need, I need. What are you doing in this body? Nothing. Have you even paid alms? I don’t have money. I saw you bought liquor last week. Brothers like that can go join them other camps out there. We don’t want you, we don’t need you here, you’re a waste of time. The righteous that are not forsaken, that lack nothing, are those doing God’s work.

sense.text: “He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.” The green pastures and still waters go into the kingdom, first and foremost; the basic answer is leading us to the kingdom. But we’re going to take it down a notch: to get to the kingdom there’s certain things we got to do and apply.

precepts.why: “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee”. That peaceful mind, a peaceful countenance, we all need, by keeping our minds stayed on the Lord. Some of you wake up fighting, you go to sleep fighting, you have a miserable mindset at home.

“When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.” Putting away childish things: going into sins, youthful lusts. That is part of what it takes to be led to the green pastures and the still waters.

“Therefore are they before the throne of God, and serve him day and night in his temple: and he that sitteth on the throne shall dwell among them”: that’s Christ. “They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more; neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat. For the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne shall feed them, and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters”.

That’s what Psalms 23, that verse 2, was talking about: he leadeth me beside the still waters. “And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes.” Christ is that living fountain of waters.

sense.text:
“He restoreth my soul”. What is that implying? We were broken. We were real broken as a people, mentally, spiritually; we were just destroyed as a people. The Lord is the only one that can restore what was taken from us. Only the Lord can restore our soul.

What happened to our soul is the curse: our children given to another people, no might, our labour eaten up, a byword among all nations, scattered, serving wood and stone. The nations took crafty counsel to cut us off from being a nation. Restoring is only for Israel, and these are the steps of it: Elijah first comes and restores all things, our identity and God’s laws; then our judges as at the first, the repairer of the breach, health and healing, the dead raised, and the times of restitution of all things.

precepts.why:
Let me give you an example: “But this is a people robbed and spoiled”. We are robbed and spoiled as a people. “They are all of them snared in holes”: we’re snared in religious and political holes. “And they are hid in prison houses”: our people are mass incarcerated. “They are for a prey”: we are for a prey to the nations, “and none delivereth”: nobody delivers the Israelites.

“For a spoil, and none saith, Restore.” Nobody says restore to them what was taken. No nation goes before the U.N., no nation goes before the world court and says, hey, you took their gold, you took their wealth, you took their identity, you took their land, you took their culture, you took their heritage, you took everything: give it back. Not one nation has stood up on our behalf. So I want y’all to see that: and none saith, Restore. Only the Lord can restore our soul.

What happened to our soul? “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long: and there shall be no might in thine hand.” When it says no might, it means no economic might, no military might, no political might. “The fruit of thy land, and all thy labours”: all our natural resources, “shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up; and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway”. This is why we need to be restored.

Read verse 37 again: “And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.”

And verse 64: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other”: we’re scattered from one side of the earth to the other in slavery. “And there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone”: even a wood cross of Jesus we would serve, and a stone of Islam. This is what it’s talking about.

I’m explaining in brief what happened to us. “They have taken crafty counsel against thy people”: the nations have taken crafty counsel against us. “And consulted against thy hidden ones”: we are the hidden ones; who we are has been hid in the earth. “They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” See that: they cut us off from being a nation.

“For they have consulted together with one consent”: the nations consulted together with one agreement. “They are confederate against thee”: all the nations are confederate against God’s people, us.

It names the nations. “The tabernacles of Edom”: the white man, that’s the Caucasians. “And the Ishmaelites”: that’s the Arabs. “Of Moab”: Moab is the Chinese. “And the Hagarenes”: the Egyptians. “Gebal”: that’s the Hamites. “And Ammon”: Ammon is the Japanese. “And Amalek”: Amalek, that’s Jewish people; they fall under Esau, Edom, too. “The Philistines”: that’s the Palestinians, “with the inhabitants of Tyre”: those are Hamites. “Assur also is joined with them”: Assur, Syria, Turkey. “They have holpen the children of Lot”: they’re helping Ammon and Moab.

Now we want to be restored. Watch what the disciples said about being restored, because the church would be like, I know, it’s about everybody being restored. No it ain’t. “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” So restoring the kingdom is only to who? Only to Israel. That’s who’s being restored: only Israel.

To get there, watch the prophecy. “Why then say the scribes that Elias must first come?” Elias is Elijah. “And Jesus answered and said unto them, Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things.” See what Elijah would do: restore all things. Restore what? Restore our identity to us, restore God’s laws to us.

“Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments.” Remember the law of Moses, my brothers and sisters. “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet”: here’s the prophecy Christ was making reference to, “before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord”: before Armageddon, before the second coming of Christ.

“And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children”: Elijah would restore your identity, Elijah would restore God’s laws to you, to keep them commandments as the Israelites. “And the heart of the children to their fathers”: we’re the children; Elijah would tell us we are the descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. That’s what Elijah would do. “Lest I come and smite the earth with a curse”: before I destroy this earth.

Us being here today is evidence that Elijah has come and gone already. Look at verse 4 so we know who it is talking about: “O Elias, how wast thou honoured in thy wondrous deeds! and who may glory like unto thee!”

Then verse 10: “Who wast ordained for reproofs in their times”: that’s God’s laws, reproofs. “To pacify the wrath of the Lord’s judgment, before it brake forth into fury”: only by us keeping God’s laws is the wrath of God’s judgment pacified. “And to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.” That’s some heavy stuff. That’s what Elijah has come and done.

He restoreth my soul; these are the steps. “And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.”

What’s heavy about that: restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning. You think back and you go, wait a minute, that was Adam and Eve. I’m just going to leave that on the table for another day.

“And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.” The restorer of paths to dwell in: that’s what we’re doing now, as Elijah has come and gone, brothers and sisters. Our mission is to restore the paths to dwell in.

“For I will restore health unto thee”: everybody’s sick and ailing, and he said, don’t worry about that, I’m going to restore health to thee. “And I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord; because they called thee an Outcast”. Outcast: God is just being nice, but that’s what it’s talking about. “Saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after”: this is Zion, that nobody gives a dag on about. So the point is, I will restore health unto thee, I will heal thee of thy wounds.

“And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her”. Don’t worry about the dead. A lot of times our mind wonders, what about those of us who have died in this truth? Don’t worry about them; they too shall be restored. “And so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed unto them.” So everything’s going to be restored.

“Let them be ashamed and confounded together that seek after my soul to destroy it; let them be driven backward and put to shame that wish me evil.” Many nations, like we read in Psalms 83, have wished us evil, and you even have amongst our own people those that wish us evil. Let them be put to shame, O Lord, that seek after my soul to destroy it.

“Repent ye therefore, and be converted”: repent ye therefore and be changed. Converted means to be changed to God’s laws. The man you was last year, you should not be that same man this year; the woman you was last year, you should not be the same woman this year. You must be converted according to God’s laws. “That your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord; And he shall send Jesus Christ, which before was preached unto you”: he’s going to send the Lord to save us, deliver us.

“Whom the heaven must receive until the times of restitution of all things”. Restitution means restoration. We’re in that time period now: this is the time of restitution, a time of restoration of all things, “which God hath spoken by the mouth of all his holy prophets since the world began.”

sense.text: “He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.” These are the steps to us being restored: we got to keep these commandments, that’s our righteousness. Christians say Christ led us to Sunday worship, Christ led us to Christmas, to Mother’s Day and Thanksgiving. No he didn’t. Keeping the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus is how he leads us in the paths of righteousness.

precepts.why: “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” So we got to keep these commandments; that’s our righteousness. That is the path of righteousness he leads us in.

Where does Christ come in? “Brethren, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.” I wanted to start at verse 1 because Christians hate to start there. The subject is Israel being saved. “For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness”: the Israelites, being ignorant of God’s righteousness, “and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.”

Verse 4 explains it: “For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.” What law did Christ end? The sacrifice of animals; he fulfilled it. Make sure in your notes you got Hebrews 10. And to every one that believeth is talking about Israel; that goes right back to verse 1.

He leads me in the paths of righteousness. “Good Master, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life? And he said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God: but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.” If you will enter into life, what? Keep the commandments. That is the path Christ leads in, not Sunday worship and Christmas.

This is leading us in the paths of righteousness, and he just sums it up right here: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.” That’s leading us in the paths of righteousness.

sense.text: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil”. Where and what is this valley? Write this down: the valley, first and foremost, is America and the lands of our captivities. The shadow of death is the darkness we sit in, bound in affliction and iron, spiritually dead in the great city, Babylon the great. The valley full of dry bones is saying the same thing with different words, and the dayspring from on high came to give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death. Psalms, Ezekiel, Revelation and Luke are all saying the same thing.

precepts.why:
“Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death”: didn’t we just read at the beginning of the class what kind of darkness? Gross darkness. “Being bound in affliction and iron”: that’s us being afflicted and in iron, in the lands of our captivity.

“Because they rebelled against the words of God”: because we rebelled against the words of God, “and contemned the counsel of the most High”: we hated the words of God, we hated the laws. “Therefore he brought down their heart with labour”: give me another word for labour, brothers: slavery. See how easy that is. “They fell down, and there was none to help”: there’s none to deliver us.

“Then they cried unto the Lord in their trouble, and he saved them out of their distresses. He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and brake their bands in sunder.” We’re waiting for that right now, brothers and sisters, because he did it before, and he shall do it again.

I said the valley’s America first and foremost, and it is. “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”. What is that great city? Babylon the great. Why does it say our dead bodies? Because we’re spiritually dead; we’re not physically dead, we are spiritually dead. “Which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.”

That great city, people ask what it is: “And there followed another angel, saying, Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city, because she made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.” Her fornication is her politics, her policies. So the great city of Revelation 11:8, where our dead bodies lie, is Babylon the great.

Why are our bodies dead in the street of the great city? “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.” That’s what makes us dead: we left the understanding of God Almighty.

I’m showing you how they all connect; they’re all saying the same thing. “The hand of the Lord was upon me, and carried me out in the spirit of the Lord, and set me down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones”. The valley full of bones is Babylon the great, where our dead bodies are; it’s saying the same thing, just using different words. “And caused me to pass by them round about: and, behold, there were very many in the open valley; and, lo, they were very dry.” Our bones here are very dry: our understanding is dry, we don’t know nothing here.

We read Luke 1 many a time, but this is what we don’t read. “To give knowledge of salvation unto his people”: the purpose of Christ is to give knowledge of salvation to his people, “by the remission of their sins”: the forgiveness of their sins. “Through the tender mercy of our God; whereby the dayspring from on high hath visited us, To give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.”

You see, it’s all saying the same thing: from Psalms, Ezekiel, Revelation, and now we’re in Luke, and it’s saying the same thing. Christ comes to give light to us in the valley of the shadow of death.

sense.text: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil”. Evil comes in many faces, sizes and facets in this world: the nations, the evil man and violent man, the evil woman, our own lust, and our own people who made a covenant with death. Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing. So I will fear no evil has various levels.

precepts.why: Evil did not start with the Greeks, but it says something about when the Greeks came in power. “And after his death they all put crowns upon themselves”: talking about Alexander’s four generals. “So did their sons after them many years: and evils were multiplied in the earth.” No, the Greeks didn’t start evil, but it was multiplied when they came in power.

I will fear no evil. “Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing”: he that keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing. “And a wise man’s heart discerneth both time and judgment”: if you’re wise, you will discern time and judgment.

Some of you hang around your drug dealer buddies or your drug user buddies, and if you hang around five drug users you’re going to be the sixth. That’s like the sister with her five girlfriends: give it time, she’ll be the sixth. I ain’t a hoe. You just give it time. You are who your circle of friends are.

Still dealing with I will fear no evil. “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man”: the evil man is the white man, the evil man is Esau, Edom. “Preserve me from the violent man”: the violent man is the white man, the violent man is Esau, Edom. “Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war”: always for war. “They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent”: that’s their media, always speaking against us. “Adders’ poison is under their lips”: their politics, their religions, is poison.

Jump down to verse 11: “Let not an evil speaker be established in the earth”: the evil speaker is the politicians and their ministers. “Evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him.” Evil’s going to hunt the violent man to overthrow him.

Still dealing with I will fear no evil. “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life: To keep thee from the evil woman, from the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman.” You didn’t know some women is evil, did you? Some of you brothers been through a horrendous divorce. You had homes and houses and cars, and now you are living in your mama’s basement because you met that good looking, big booty, big breasted evil woman.

Brother, a woman will flatter you to death to get what she wants. You might be four foot two, she’ll make you think you’re six foot three. You might be 400 pounds of whale blubber, but if you got something she want, she’ll make you think you are an Adonis, muscles for days. You might be skin and bones, she’ll make you think you look like Arnold Schwarzenegger. And she will fool you and get everything you got, and then you are crushed and destroyed.

There was a brother in Atlanta, the same thing. She ain’t for you. No Bishop, you wrong, she for me. Time went by and she took the money out of his bank account, got into his VA benefits, put her name on it, changed the code and blocked him out and got all the funds. He went back with the woman anyway, and then he found her diary and found out she been sleeping with everybody. Now he’s doing videos cursing us out, rather than saying, brother, y’all was right. All we did was warn you. I’ve seen this movie before. When your spiritual eyes are open you can discern time and judgment: this is going to happen, brother, here are the signs. Brother, you weak and you are simple. You’re simple as hell. So women can be evil.

There’s a woman online talking about men could be evil too. Yeah they can, but we ain’t talking about that right now; don’t change the subject. “And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.” The men started to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. “And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods”: the men started to worship their gods. “And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.” The Lord was mad with us.

“And the Lord said unto Moses, Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel.” So God told Moses, kill everybody that did this thing; kill them all.

“And Moses said unto the judges of Israel, Slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baal–peor.” Did God say, I will restore your judges as at the first? Remember that. So if you was the officer of ten and you knew five of your men did this thing, you had to kill them. If you was a captain of a hundred and 98 of your men did this, what you had to do. Under every judge, every officer, captain, you had men unto you, and you had to know the state of the flock of those men.

That history ain’t over yet. Who did we commit whoredom with? “And Moses was wroth with the officers of the host, with the captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, which came from the battle. And Moses said unto them, Have ye saved all the women alive?” I see a whole lot of women that y’all saved alive.

“Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.” Moses reveals something heavy. Brother, y’all thought the women loved you: no, them women didn’t love you. There was a plot. Balaam said, we cannot overcome the Israelites, but I got a plan: send those women amongst those men, let those women make them believe they are the cream of the crop, the creme de la creme, and these dumb, stupid Israelite men, yeah baby, I got it going on, get them to sin and you can kill them. And that’s what happened.

It’s the same battle strategy today with the NBA, the NFL, the entire entertainment world. They always send in women of other nations: white women, or China, or whatever the hell they are; they’re not our people. Marriage is a political thing, brothers; it’s a strategy, because when he dies she gets his money and that money goes back to her family. A lot of these women are Amalek.

And they get rid of the ratchet wife too. In the entertainment world they say, bring your wife around, we want to meet her, and if she’s ratchet, tats on her face, can’t construct a sentence, she can’t be around the other wives at the parties; get rid of her, we got women for you, any kind you want. Like in the movie Devil’s Advocate: before he signed, they needed to meet his wife. Everything hinges on you and your wife, because she is a reflection of you. Some of you brothers are scared to bring your wife around because she’s ratchet; she reveals the simp in you. You don’t become president of the United States without them meeting your wife and your family. Guess what, brothers: it’s the same with God.

You may be saying that’s only in the world, that’s not in Jesus. Watch: “For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?” Y’all know that. You’re scared to bring your wife around, you know she’s a ratchet hood rat, she is a chicken head. It’s the same with God: a man that can’t rule his own house can’t take care of the church of God.

This is what Solomon’s mama taught him, and this is what we are teaching you via Solomon’s mama; his nickname is Lemuel. “Give not thy strength unto women”. How many of you will admit you have given your strength to women? What does it mean, giving your strength to a woman? It means giving her the power over you, and access to all of your resources, money. Exactly.

Now a scripture about a man that gave his strength to a woman. “Yea, many there be that have run out of their wits for women”: some of you brothers, if you have given your strength to a woman, you will lose your mind. “And become servants for their sakes”: you will become servants to the woman. “Many also have perished, have erred, and sinned, for women.” Many of you have died, have erred, made mistakes and sinned for women. That’s a simp right there.

That’s what Lemuel’s mama, Solomon’s mama, said: don’t give your strength to a woman. You don’t give her your mind, you don’t give her your spirit, you don’t give her your resources, you don’t give her nothing. And the ones that’s mad are the ratchet ones who ain’t got nothing, always looking to get what you got; the insecure ones that destroy what you got so they can take it, live lovely, and make everybody believe they worked hard for it. No, you destroyed a soul for what you got.

Brother, never move in with a woman. If that’s her house, her apartment, her name, as soon as she gets an attitude, or she meets the next one that got better swag than you, you are out the door. You ain’t a man if you move in with her; she got to move in with you.

“Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God”: when that big booty woman comes around, don’t say God is doing this to me. “For God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” His own lust: that’s something within you, brother; that’s something within you, sister, something you lack, something you want. The single sister knows what I’m talking about: I ain’t had none in five years. You don’t need none; go take a bath and lose some weight, get yourself together. And the brother can’t even take care of himself, can’t put two sentences together: I want a woman. And do what with her?

“Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” Brothers, sisters, y’all playing with death. All I can do is warn you: you are playing with death. So I will fear no evil has various levels.

Brothers and sisters often ask, what about those that die? Death is always a big topic. “The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart”: men and women that keep the commandments do die in this truth. “And merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.”

Some people die because the Lord is being merciful, to prevent them from the evil that’s going to come their way. It’s not that the brother or sister was wicked. He said, I’m being merciful on this spirit right here, because evil’s going to come their way; I’m going to have them pass on. And passing on in that death means they’re going to get their new body, their celestial body.

I’m still dealing with fear no evil. “Because ye have said”: because Israelite leaders have said, “We have made a covenant with death”: we made a covenant with the white man; death is symbolic for the white man. “And with hell are we at agreement”: with the low condition of our people. “When the overflowing scourge shall pass through”: when judgment shall pass through, “it shall not come unto us”: they say nothing’s going to happen to us. Why? “For we have made lies our refuge”: you believe in white man Jesus, so ain’t nothing going to happen to us. “And under falsehood have we hid ourselves”: it’s Christianity.

“Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste. Judgment also will I lay to the line, and righteousness to the plummet: and the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies”: Christian lies, political lies shall be swept away. “And the waters shall overflow the hiding place.”

“And your covenant with death shall be disannulled”: your agreement with the white man shall be disannulled. “And your agreement with hell shall not stand; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, then ye shall be trodden down by it.” All you men and women making agreement with white society, American society, to aid and abet the destruction of your people: when it goes down, you go down too. That’s what the Lord is prophesying right there.

Here’s an example, during the time of the Greeks. “In those days went there out of Israel wicked men”: so we know amongst our own people, the Israelites, there were wicked men, “who persuaded many, saying, Let us go and make a covenant with the heathen that are round about us”: the nations, the Greeks. That’s why we read in Isaiah, we made a covenant with death, and with hell we are at agreement. Here’s the example of it: “for since we departed from them we have had much sorrow.”

“Then came ungodly persons, who hated their own people, went unto the king, and told him that Jonathan besieged the tower”. You see that: you had certain people that hated their own people, and these are Israelites. As it was true back then, it’s true today.

I’m still showing you how they made a covenant with death, and with hell they had agreement. “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

So they made an agreement with Rome for their position, their placements, their position in society. That’s how they got those seats of authority, through Rome. As it was true back then, it is true today: our people who are in politics and in religion, Rome, America, gave them those seats of authority.

sense.text: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil”. We briefly went over what evil is, in its various forms; now a little more on evil. Remember, the things that occurred before time were written for our learning, because they will occur again. The same people that gathered together against Christ, and against the apostles and the followers of Christ, you think they’re dead and gone: they’re back today.

precepts.why:
“Who by the mouth of thy servant David hast said, Why did the heathen rage, and the people imagine vain things? The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord, and against his Christ.” He’s quoting Psalms chapter 2. “For of a truth against thy holy child Jesus, whom thou hast anointed, both Herod, and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles, and the people of Israel, were gathered together”.

In verse 27, Herod and Pontius Pilate with the Gentiles and the people of Israel were gathered together: they made an agreement to destroy Christ. And Peter and them mentioned it because those same people made an agreement to kill the apostles, to kill the followers of Christ. You think they’re dead and gone; they’re back today.

“And Saul was consenting unto his death. And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.”

This is why we’re trying to gear you men up, with your passports, to assist us in traveling. But we’re only going to choose those men who are diligent, loyal, and prove themselves studied in the scriptures, not just any old random do-nothing brother. When they were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, they knew them places, because they traveled there before. Things are going to go down, and men need to be circumspect of locations and areas. You ain’t going to stop this truth.

We ain’t picking nobody that murmurs; if your house is out of order, if your wife has a reputation of being a murmurer, don’t even think about it. “Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.”

sense.text:
“Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil.” We went through in brief some evil plots and plans: mind war, silent weaponry, their plan to destroy blacks and Hispanics. That is their goal, that is their outset. But we have the word of God. “For thou art with me”: the Lord is with us.

“Thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.” When the Bible talks about the rod, it is the rod of correction. The rod is whooping that behind, but from God’s standpoint. The staff is used to uphold you; we call it a cane today. So it is the rod of correction and the staff of support, and they comfort me.

precepts.why: What does it mean, “thy rod”? “Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.” The rod of correction: when it says thy rod and thy staff they comfort me, the rod is whooping that behind. That is what it is talking about, but it is from God’s standpoint.
“Withhold not correction from the child: for if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.” So the rod is used for beatings, for whippings.

“It is good for me that I have been afflicted; that I might learn thy statutes.” There is a purpose behind God afflicting us. There is a purpose behind God’s rod whooping us for our sins: that we might learn his statutes, learn his law.

The rod brings tribulation, and there is glory in it: “we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.”

An example of the rod: how your earthly father beats you, and how God beats us. “For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.”

“Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us”: that deals with the rod. Those scriptures in Proverbs are your earthly father beating you. “And we gave them reverence”: when your father beat you it was not to destroy you, it was to teach you lessons in life. Don’t do this, don’t do that, do it this way.

“Shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?” If we gave reverence to our earthly fathers who beat us, and they were not trying to kill us, we have to give much more honor to the Father of spirits, the God of heaven and earth, our heavenly father.

The staff: a staff is used to uphold you. It was a custom in Israel to walk around with a staff, but especially when you got old; we call it a cane today. “There shall yet old men and old women dwell in the streets of Jerusalem, and every man with his staff in his hand for very age.” When you are up in age you would have a staff. So thy rod and thy staff they comfort me: the rod of correction and the staff of support.
“They comfort me.” “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

Still dealing with they comfort me. “Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God.” Speak comfortably to Jerusalem, “and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished”, that her iniquity is pardoned: God has forgiven us. “For she hath received of the Lord’s hand double for all her sins.”

So we are to comfort our people. We are telling them the truth: our warfare is accomplished, Christ died for our sins, our iniquities are wiped away. So now all we have to do is prepare ourselves.

sense.text:
“Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies.” That table is the book, the Bible: God wrote it before them in a table and noted it in a book. And what was written there he sets in order before the eyes, before the eyes of our enemies.

“Thou anointest my head with oil.” When your head gets anointed with oil you start to think on another level: you shall see your desire on your enemies. My enemies need to go down, they need to be destroyed. Christians say you have to forgive everybody; that is not Bible.

precepts.why: What is this table? “Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever.” Note it in a book: that is the Bible. That is the table it is talking about.

“These things hast thou done, and I kept silence.” God kept silent at the evils that America and Esau have done to us. “Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” Then: “Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.”

That is the part wanted: I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes. Read Psalms 23:5 again: “Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies.” That is what Psalms 50 says. He sets them in order before the eyes, before the eyes of our enemies.

Thou anointest my head with oil, and here is the precept. “But my horn shalt thou exalt like the horn of an unicorn”: the unicorn the Bible speaks of is a rhinoceros. “I shall be anointed with fresh oil.”

“Mine eye also shall see my desire on mine enemies, and mine ears shall hear my desire of the wicked that rise up against me.” Some of y’all don’t want that. That is why Christians say all the time you have to forgive everybody, forgive and forget. What you are saying is not Bible. That is what the Bible is saying, and that is when your head gets anointed with oil: you start to think on another level. My enemies need to go down, they need to be destroyed, today God, today destroy them. You have to send them prayers constantly.

Then: “The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree: he shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon.”

That is why, when brothers and sisters died, they cried under the altar. “And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held: And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true”, dost thou not “judge and avenge our blood”?

Our forefathers and foremothers cry for that: judge and avenge our blood. That is not taught in church. Nobody teaches that in church, because they say that is not of Jesus. Shut the hell up. That is seeing your desire on your enemies, the anointing of Psalms 92 and Psalms 23.

sense.text: “Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever.” It is basically explaining itself, but there is deep understanding in it. Psalms 23 is about dwelling in the house of the Lord: the one the Lord chooses to approach unto him, the Jerusalem he builds up after the captivity, and the city whose gates are never shut, which only those written in the Lamb’s book of life will enter.

precepts.why: “One thing have I desired of the Lord, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the Lord, and to enquire in his temple.”

“Blessed is the man whom thou choosest, and causest to approach unto thee.” You can’t just walk up to the Lord on his throne; he has to choose you to approach before him. That is order, that is discipline, that is honor, that is structure. You don’t say, I’m just going to go see the Lord. You don’t do that.

“That he may dwell in thy courts: we shall be satisfied with the goodness of thy house, even of thy holy temple.”

“And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”: come on, Jerusalem. “And their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee”: slavery, oppression, colonialism, loss of identity. “But in my favour have I had mercy on thee”: that is Christ dying on a cross, and this captivity having an end.

“Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles.” The word forces means their wealth. “And that their kings may be brought”: their kings are going to be brought in chains. “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.” The churches don’t teach that; they skip over that.

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together”: the sanctuary is going to be built up, “and I will make the place of my feet glorious.” This is the house of the Lord that Psalms 23 says we will dwell in for ever.

Back to Isaiah 60:11: “Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night.” Here is the precept, brothers, write this down. “And the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there. And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it. And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.”

So who is written in the Lamb’s book of life? Christians say everybody that believes in white Jesus. Isaiah 4:3 shows whether that is true.

Who is written in the Lamb’s book of life? “And it shall come to pass, that he that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem.” Everyone that is written among the living in Jerusalem.

Back to Revelation 21:27: there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, “but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.” The ones written in the Lamb’s book of life are those written among the living in Jerusalem, not everybody that believes in white Jesus. They are the ones who will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever. So brothers, never give up.
